content:
Multiplication starts in Class 2 with equal groups, arrays and the 2–10 tables — core content for the Maths Olympiad Class 2 syllabus. Here is what it tests, the facts to memorise, the common mix-ups, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 2 Maths Olympiad Multiplication chapter tests

  • Equal groups and repeated addition (4 + 4 + 4 = 3 × 4)
  • Arrays (rows × columns)
  • Multiplication tables 2 to 10 and multiplication facts
  • Word problems with "each", "every" and "groups of"

Key facts your child should know

  • 3 × 4 = 12 is 3 groups of 4, the same as 4 + 4 + 4.
  • Order does not matter: 3 × 4 = 4 × 3.
  • × 1 leaves a number unchanged; × 0 gives 0.
  • An array of r rows and c columns has r × c items.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Adding instead of multiplying for equal groups.
  • Miscounting a table fact (e.g. 7 × 8).
  • Reversing rows and columns yet expecting a different answer.

quiz.title: IMO Class 2 Multiplication Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: A classroom has 4 rows of 7 desks and 3 more desks near the door. How many desks are there?
questions.explanation: Rows first: 4 × 7 = 28 desks. Add the extra 3: 28 + 3 = 31.

questions.q: Which number does NOT come in the table of 6: 24, 36, 44, 54?
questions.explanation: 24 = 6 × 4, 36 = 6 × 6 and 54 = 6 × 9, but no number times 6 gives 44.

questions.q: An album page holds 10 stamps. Ishan fills 3 pages and has 7 loose stamps. How many stamps does he have?
questions.explanation: Rows first: 3 × 10 = 30 stamps. Add the extra 7: 30 + 7 = 37.

questions.q: A farm has 2 spiders and 3 ants. Each of the spiders has 8 legs and each of the ants has 6 legs. How many legs are there in all?
Each of the stools has 3 legs. How many legs do 8 stools have altogether?
Kavya has 3 vases with 9 roses in each. How many roses are there in all?
A farm has 6 cats and 5 pigeons. Each of the cats has 4 legs and each of the pigeons has 2 legs. How many legs are there in all?
A packet has 8 biscuits. Riya takes 5 packets to school and shares 2 packets equally between two class parties. How many biscuits does EACH party get?
questions.explanation: 2 packets have 2 × 8 = 16 biscuits. Split equally in two: 8 each.

questions.q: Ravi knows 6 × 9 = 54. Without multiplying again, what is 9 × 6?
questions.explanation: Turning the numbers around does not change the product: 9 × 6 = 6 × 9 = 54.

faq.a: Multiplication is repeated addition of equal groups: 3 × 4 means 4 added three times, which is 12.

faq.q: Does the order matter in multiplication?
faq.a: No. 3 × 4 and 4 × 3 both equal 12 — that is the order (commutative) rule.
